 Spiritual

¶4:**

This
 principle

 be understood
 by
 comparing
 two
 operations
 upon
 the interior
 life
. If an
 advers
a
rial fals
ity,
 hostile
 to the mind
, ass

 the understanding
 and

icts corruption
 and
 injury

 spiritual man
 —
 and
 then

aults it
 a

ounding its

ort
ions upon
 the
 already
-damaged
 states
,
 so
 that fals
ity is

ered upon falsity, and the
 harm
 is
 red
oubled — then the whole
 accus
ation against

 destruct
ive fals
ity is brought
 before
 the Divine
 Order

erns all

 exam
ines the fals
ity directly
, according
 to the

 of

 it

 life

 the evidence

 the

 seat
 of perception

 fals
ity is led
 into
 judgment
 according
 to the
 eternal
 law of consequences
, and is condemned
 before the Divine Government
 of
 all
 things
. The penalty
 answers
 exactly
 to the injury
:
 corruption
 is
 met
 with dissolution
 in
 the very place where it corru
pted,
 and the full
 measure
 of harm

icted upon

 who had committed
 no
 prior
 offense

 is

emnation.
 The Divine
 Order does not omit any
 consequence

ary;
 it
 is judged precisely
 according to the
 
enmity it
 carried
 within
 itself.

---


**¶5:**
When
 that
 process
 is completed, the
 hostile
 falsity stands
 condemned according
 to the
 full
 r
eckoning of its destruct
ive action
. But
 afterward
, the one
 who was
 ass
aulted —
 the interior
 life
 that
 was har
med — remains
 in
 a state of spiritual
 inf
irmity.
 The injury
 dealt
 by
 fals
ity brings
 forth further
 disorder
 from
 within
, and the person
 becomes spiritu
ally sick from
 what
 has
 been
 lod
ged in
 the will
 and
 understanding
. Then
 the Divine Truth
 that heals is called upon
,
 and the wound
 of
 the
 spiritual life is laid
 open
 before
 it
. Yet
 this healing Truth
 poss
esses neither
 mal
ice nor host
ility; it takes
 the sharp
,
 discriminating power
 of pure
 truth
 and
 opens
 the wound
.
 And
 when
 it
 opens
 it, the living
 truth
 within
 —
 which
 had
 been trapped and
 corrupted —
 p
ours forth
 from
 the place
 of injury.
 The person suf
fers pain in
 this
 operation
, yet
 accepts both
 the cutting
 and the out
pouring,
 because
 the Divine
 Truth that heals has
 not acted
 from
 
enmity,
 and
 no
 destruct
ive intent
 was imposed
 upon the
 one who suf
fers.
 Everything
 that the
 healing
 Truth does
,
 it does for the restoration
 of spiritual
 whol
eness —
 entirely
 for the sake
 of good
, and
 never
 from
 the
 intention
 of evil
.

---

**¶6
:**
When
 the operation
 is complete
 —
 when
 the discrimin
ating truth has opened
 the place
 of corruption
 and
 released
 what
 was confined
 within it
 and
 restored
 sound
ness to the spiritual
 life — then the one
 who was he
aled offers
 the
 in
most
 acknowledg
ments
 of gratitude and
 love
. The
 very
 illness
 and its
 healing become a testimony
 to the power
 of Divine
 Truth,
 and that
 truth
 is honored and
 glor
ified in
 the sight
 of all
 who perce
ive it.

---

**
¶7:**
This is
 precisely
 how the
 matter
 stands
 with
 respect
 to the living interior
 soul —
 the
 capt
ive wisdom
 within
 every
 created
 being. When
 the operations
 of truth
 reach
 it
 in
 the fullness of time
, though
 the cutting
 is
 painful
, whol
eness and peace
 come
 to ab
ide in it
 at
 last
. And
 a
 spiritual
 glory arises from this very
 process of healing,
 for
 what
 once
 suffered
 now
 test
ifies to the power that
 restored
 it. The pain
 was
 real
, but it
 was the
 pain of liberation
.


---

**¶8:**

By
 contrast
, the other
 principle
 — the hostile
 falsity that struck
 the interior
 life — acted
 from
 cr
uelty alone
. Its
 assault
 upon
 the living
 soul carried
 no intention
 of healing
 and
 no prospect
 of restoration. It struck
 from
 
enmity, being
 cruel according to its
 very
 nature, and therefore
 the full
 accus
ation of spiritual
 law
 stands
 against
 it.

---

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: After the end, this enemy is condemned for the retaliation [of his] sin against him. Afterwards, the other one is sick [still,] the one whom this enemy has struck, and a wound comes out on him [from within,] and he becomes a sick person by cause of his illness, and he [is in great distress.] He calls the doctor and shows him his wound. However, that doctor has no [malice] nor [enmity,] and he takes the knife to him and cuts this wound. Nevertheless, when he cuts it the blood shall pour out of his wound. That person shall be pained, but he accepts those and these things. This doctor has not retaliated nor was harm imposed on him; because he did this thing to him for healing his wound. All that he did to him was done for the good; and not directly for evil.

After the completion, he cuts this wound and lets blood from it and heals it. He shall even make [to him] gifts and compliments. That illness and the healing become a pride for this doctor, and he is given honour.

Also, [this] is the other person [who] struck the comrade of the [first; he made him] sick with his [blows.] he struck in [enmity,] he being cruel according to [his evil nature. And the] living soul [bears witness] upon it[, so] that [the full] accusation of [the law stands against him.]

This is
 also how this matter of [the healing
 stands] before this living soul. [
It is like the work of the doctor
.] At the time [when]
 it [comes about that] you have
 struck [and cut the wound,]
 it is well and [peace and]
 ease shall exist for it. [And
] A glory comes about for this [
one through the] healing[, and
] it exists [in wholeness,
 though] it is painful [at first
.]

For this matter is like to two people, if a personal enemy and an opponent of theirs will hit one first and make a sore and a wound on his body. Afterwards he smites him again and [...] and he hits over his blows and [...] blows that have made sores on him and [...] strikes him these two times [...] accuses his enemy who has struck him. And this judge questions him to his face about the [...] of the sores that he has left as marks on his body. And they [...] on him as if he had split his head. And he is led to judgement and sentence, and is punished before the judge of the world. He makes retribution for a sore in the sore place, and adds to him the wound that he had left on this person who had not yet sinned against him. He shall not omit the retaliation of the opponent, as he is judged [...] according to enmity.
